title.narrative: Provision of Emergency Lifesaving Nutrition Essential Package Services for Children Under-five and Pregnant and Lactating Women in Afgooye District, Lower Shabelle Region, South West State of Somalia

description.narrative: ltpgtSomalia Young Doctors Association (SOYDA) proposes a 12-month, life-saving nutrition intervention in Afgooye District, Lower Shabelle, in response to the SHF Reserve Allocation – December 2025: Drought Response in Southern Somalia. Prolonged drought, food insecurity, displacement, and disease outbreaks have significantly increased the risk of acute malnutrition and excess mortality among children under five (CU5) and pregnant and lactating women (PLW), requiring urgent, scalable action.ltbrgtltspangtThe project aims to reduce morbidity and mortality related to acute malnutrition through an integrated package of early detection, referral, treatment, and prevention services, in line with SHF life-saving priorities and the Somalia Nutrition Cluster response framework.lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltspangtSOYDA will implement multi-layered nutrition screening and identification using Mass MUAC campaigns, Family MUAC, routine CHW-led household screening, and systematic screening at supported health facilities to ensure early case detection and high coverage in drought-affected communities. All identified cases will be promptly referred to appropriate services.lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtSevere Acute Malnutrition (SAM) cases without complications will receive treatment through health facility–based Outpatient Therapeutic Programme (OTP) services integrated within MCH platforms, while complicated cases will be referred to Stabilization Centres. Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM) among CU5 and PLW will be managed through Targeted Supplementary Feeding Programmes (TSFP), complemented by micronutrient supplementation and promotion of improved home diets.ltbrgtltspangtPrevention efforts will be strengthened through facility- and community-based IYCF counselling and the Care Group Approach, integrating key nutrition-sensitive messaging on hygiene, health, and immunization. Protection mainstreaming will be ensured through application of the Child Protection and Nutrition Integration Framework, PSEA/GBV training, and referral pathways. Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP) mechanisms will ensure community participation, feedback, and program responsiveness.lt/spangtlt/pgt
